what: The heuristic precomputes customer/depot fact encodings and a routing-cost matrix from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operators using their metric costs. It optionally resolves exact `load()`, `capacity()`, and per-customer `demand(...)` PNEs, degrading to unlimited capacity and zero unknown demand when folded PNEs are absent. At evaluation, it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes a Prim MST over the depot, current location, and remaining customers, and constructs a nearest-neighbour completion that inserts depot route breaks when known capacity is exhausted. The returned estimate is 80% greedy completion cost plus 20% MST cost; completed customer sets outside the depot return the exact remaining return cost.
why: CVRP states require both global routing awareness and sensitivity to the currently open vehicle route. The MST component cheaply captures the spatial connectivity of all remaining customers, while the greedy completion models the mandatory final depot return and likely route breaks caused by capacity. The representative instances have dense metric-like travel graphs and widely varying capacities and vehicle counts, making operator-derived distances more reliable than translated PNE names and making capacity-aware route closure especially useful when resource PNEs survive translation. Blending the two estimates reduces nearest-neighbour instability while remaining inexpensive at the target instance sizes.
